name: Cinereous
lede: Cinereous is an old word for ashen grey, used above all of birds, and Ridgway's own swatch for it is a plain grey.

sections.title: Ashen, especially of birds
sections.body: Paterson defines cinereous as grey and ashen, ash grey, especially of birds, and lists related words: cinerescent for becoming ashen, and cineritious for ashy-grey as applied to nerve matter [1]. The color name entered our sources through Ridgway's 1886 nomenclature, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 carried it over [2]. Compare [[ash]], [[grey]] and [[mouse-grey]].

sections.title: Two swatches
sections.body: The swatch here is a warm, brownish grey, nearest ISCC-NBS name "light grayish reddish brown" at a distance of 2.8 [2]. Ridgway's 1912 plate LII shows his own cinereous as #AAACAB, a neutral grey [2]. The sources disagree on screen color, so read the name as ashen and not as a precise tint. See also [[taupe]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch appears in 305 of our 23,781 paintings, 1.28 percent, as photographed [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, found in 39 of the 1,674 paintings from that century, 2.7 times the expected rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color [3]. The most devoted painter is Maurice Denis, with 6 of his 43 works here, 7.4 times the baseline of the museums those works come from [3].
